top_reviews.title: I love this phone a lot, totally worth the money
top_reviews.variant: Color: Violet Shadow Size: 512GB Style: Fold8 Ultra Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: Amazon delivered this phone to me earlier than scheduled. They just need me to be at home because this is a high-valued item so it’s fair enough. I’m glad to be at home to receive this phone. This is my third time buying phones on Amazon. It’s simple and easy to receive it. I don’t understand why others people said negatively about it. They even give me high value for trade in, and give me extra $400 for rebate credit. And $350 Amazon gift card. What a great great deal for a new phone like this. Secondly, once I use foldable phone, I don’t want to go back to normal phone because it helps me with lots of things , totally worth the money like multitasking with 3 tasks at the same time, reading books like a mini ipad, watching movies and videos better with larger screen, and importantly I can take pictures or record videos myself by using main camera and I still can see myself on the screen, fast processing. This camera is far better than previous models because it has upgraded camera perfectly to be a high-quality one, pretty the same to its flagship S26 ultra that’s why I decided to change to this phone. I think Samsung is the leader in foldable phone right now. About the battery, if you use Samsung charger, it takes way faster to charge the phone to 100%, I mean way faster than Apple. And the battery can last through the whole day. I used my phone a lot in the day, at the end of the day my phone still at 40% battery. The display and sound are excellent too. The displays both front and inside are very bright even under the sunlight. Overall, I love using this phone and I feel ecstatic to buy this phone. It’s a great choice for me, never regret.

top_reviews.title: A great phone, though pricey
top_reviews.variant: Color: Graphite Size: 512GB Style: Fold8 Ultra Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: The Fold 8 Ultra isn't my first foldable phone. My first is its older sibling, the Fold 5. The Fold 5 was a great phone in many ways. The Fold 8 Ultra improved on the Fold 5 in many ways. The chief thing is that it is a light phone. Another thing is that when folded it feels like a normal phone. It is perhaps very slightly thicker than a typical slate phone. We're talking about mm thicker, tops. The magic happens when you open the phone to the bigger inner screen. The crease on my Fold 8 Ultra is hardly noticeable. I can barely feel it or see it unless light hits it at just an angle. As of writing this review I've owned the Fold 8 Ultra for a little over a month now and this has remained true. We'll see if the crease remains this unnoticeable in time. Another thing is the battery. I can get away with two days on a single charge if I use the phone normally. If I use it a bit more heavily I can get by on one charge for the entire day. In addition, should I need to charge the phone pronto it can be fast charged with 45 watt charging. I charge mine with my fold 5's charger, which is a 25 watt charger. It is plenty. Besides all that it is a gorgeous looking phone. It looks sharp and elegant from a glance. I get many questions about it - even from people that have seen me with a Fold 5. Not that getting attention is important for a phone, but it is as it is. In total, a great phone.

top_reviews.title: The best foldable. Excellent smartphone + mini tablet in one
top_reviews.variant: Color: Violet Shadow Size: 512GB Style: Fold8 Ultra Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: Went from Fold 3 to Fold 8. Firstly, this fold pretty much fixed any issue I had with foldables. Thin Lightweight Good Battery Quick charging Good Camera Less crease Inner display is bright outdoors for viewing. With phone closed, you can use front display as a smartphone normally. It unfolds into a mini tablet experience. Phone is durable and feels good in hands. Software is very good and everything works well for android, minus a few quirks. Lots of features to try out and customize. Main complaint is now camera bump (phone does not lay flat). And the selfie camera holes. This is simply the best foldable. Easily the best phone. And most portable mini tablet ever. Samsungs finest thus far.

top_reviews.title: Love the foldable design
top_reviews.variant: Color: Graphite Size: 256GB Style: Fold8 Ultra Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: I really like the foldable screen. It’s convenient for multitasking and watching videos, and the camera takes clear photos. Overall, I’m happy with it.

top_reviews.title: Best foldable on the international market.
top_reviews.variant: Color: Violet Shadow Size: 512GB Style: Fold8 Ultra Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: The phone has exceeded my expectations and has been nothing but a treat, I've been using it everyday non stop, the crease is as good as the oppo find n6 as well as processing power. The camera quality isn't a major upgrade for me as I cam from the S-- Ultra series but the outcomes of the pics I've took so far are more than exceptional, especially with one ui 9 and the enhanced AI features and capabilities. I would definitely recommend this phone, I am a little sad about no pen support but after a few days of use for work and personal, the pen didn't become something I would have required, the 8 inch inner display is enough.

top_reviews.title: Buy it!
top_reviews.variant: Color: Violet Shadow Size: 512GB Style: Fold8 Ultra Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: This is the best phone I've ever used. I love how thin it is and it's a slim phone when closed and can open to a tablet when needed. Paired mine with a Rokform case and it's perfect. This is my first foldable and don't think I'll be going back to a traditional phone slab. Little pricey but from what you get I think its worth the bundle you get in one form factor.

top_reviews.title: If you have the disposable funds and you really want a foldable...this is for you!
top_reviews.variant: Color: Violet Shadow Size: 512GB Style: Fold8 Ultra Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: Good unit albeit an expensive one. If this is the first purchase of a foldable android that has the normal dimensions of a mainstream bar type cell phone, this Samsung is quite good, bright screen, easier to open, crease in the middle is minimal, screen is not highly reflective, good battery, powerful unit. I own a Fold 7 and although the Fold 8 Ultra is better in the areas aforementioned, it is not so much better that one needs to spend over $2K on a replacement a year later. These devices still need babysitting because they are highly subject to damage form dust and water which compromises durability. However, if money is not an issue this device is a prime device in its class in this country. I am not going to cover the technical specifications because most buyers are hardly likely to utilize the device beyond it's primary functions and those are the ones most obvious that I have mentioned. If I did not own the Fold 7, I would probably have kept the unit but I returned the 8, not because it was not a great and attractive device but because it was not a $1000 better than the device I have and the trade in value of my less than 1 year old device was 50% depreciation which was unreasonable. The Fold 8 Ultra is a nice device but I am not sure that it is really worth the cost...Amazon's offering is outstanding with the gift card so if the offer is still available and you really want the device the Amazon offer is WAYYY better than Samsung's which is really them upselling another device simultaneously. Good luck if you decide you have the disposable income to spend it on this device. Not 5 stars on the rating because of the cost...one other thing...there is still a crease in the middle of the unfolded screen just in case you are wondering.

top_reviews.body: The Fold 8 Ultra isn't my first foldable phone. My first is its older sibling, the Fold 5. The Fold 5 was a great phone in many ways. The Fold 8 Ultra improved on the Fold 5 in many ways. The chief thing is that it is a light phone. Another thing is that when folded it feels like a normal phone. It is perhaps very slightly thicker than a typical slate phone. We're talking about mm thicker, tops. The magic happens when you open the phone to the bigger inner screen. The crease on my Fold 8 Ultra is hardly noticeable. I can barely feel it or see it unless light hits it at just an angle. As of writing this review I've owned the Fold 8 Ultra for a little over a month now and this has remained true. We'll see if the crease remains this unnoticeable in time. Another thing is the battery. I can get away with two days on a single charge if I use the phone normally. If I use it a bit more heavily I can get by on one charge for the entire day. In addition, should I need to charge the phone pronto it can be fast charged with 45 watt charging. I charge mine with my fold 5's charger, which is a 25 watt charger. It is plenty. Besides all that it is a gorgeous looking phone. It looks sharp and elegant from a glance. I get many questions about it - even from people that have seen me with a Fold 5. Not that getting attention is important for a phone, but it is as it is. In total, a great phone.

What are the key features of Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra
Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra combines a premium foldable design with powerful performance, advanced photography and AI features. The thinner and lighter design is just 4.1 millimeters thick when unfolded and weighs 215 grams.
What is the difference between Galaxy Z Fold7 and Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra?
Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra features some improvements to the design and camera system that deliver durability and high-quality videos when shooting.
What is the difference between Galaxy Z Fold8 and Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra?
As our product line evolves, our original Z Fold model has advanced to become Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra and the Z Fold8 model has been resdesigned with an all-new shape.
I’m switching to Galaxy for the first time. How easy is it?
The excitement of finding your perfect foldable phone can also bring up anxiety about switching from iPhone. Bring over photos, contacts and passwords. Share files and encrypt messages in a way you’re used to. And do it all on Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra.
How durable is Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra?
Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra is fortified with material that strengthen the device for long-lasting durability. The Armor Aluminum frame provides enhanced protection for the device's internal components and exterior edges without adding excessive bulk.

top_reviews.title: Dope phone
top_reviews.variant: Color: Graphite Size: 512GB Style: Fold8 Ultra Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: Upgraded from s22 ultra and yes its more fragile, but worth it. Youll take care of it because youll enjoy how aesthetically pleasing it is and how cool this thing is to hold. I love it. The sound quality is a bit lacking though and the picture quality isnt that good, but performance, and build quality is top tier. Awesome phone. I will.be a foldable guy from now on. So cool no lie.

top_reviews.title: I love this phone a lot, totally worth the money
top_reviews.variant: Color: Violet Shadow Size: 512GB Style: Fold8 Ultra Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: Amazon delivered this phone to me earlier than scheduled. They just need me to be at home because this is a high-valued item so it’s fair enough. I’m glad to be at home to receive this phone. This is my third time buying phones on Amazon. It’s simple and easy to receive it. I don’t understand why others people said negatively about it. They even give me high value for trade in, and give me extra $400 for rebate credit. And $350 Amazon gift card. What a great great deal for a new phone like this. Secondly, once I use foldable phone, I don’t want to go back to normal phone because it helps me with lots of things , totally worth the money like multitasking with 3 tasks at the same time, reading books like a mini ipad, watching movies and videos better with larger screen, and importantly I can take pictures or record videos myself by using main camera and I still can see myself on the screen, fast processing. This camera is far better than previous models because it has upgraded camera perfectly to be a high-quality one, pretty the same to its flagship S26 ultra that’s why I decided to change to this phone. I think Samsung is the leader in foldable phone right now. About the battery, if you use Samsung charger, it takes way faster to charge the phone to 100%, I mean way faster than Apple. And the battery can last through the whole day. I used my phone a lot in the day, at the end of the day my phone still at 40% battery. The display and sound are excellent too. The displays both front and inside are very bright even under the sunlight. Overall, I love using this phone and I feel ecstatic to buy this phone. It’s a great choice for me, never regret.

top_reviews.title: A great phone, though pricey
top_reviews.variant: Color: Graphite Size: 512GB Style: Fold8 Ultra Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: The Fold 8 Ultra isn't my first foldable phone. My first is its older sibling, the Fold 5. The Fold 5 was a great phone in many ways. The Fold 8 Ultra improved on the Fold 5 in many ways. The chief thing is that it is a light phone. Another thing is that when folded it feels like a normal phone. It is perhaps very slightly thicker than a typical slate phone. We're talking about mm thicker, tops. The magic happens when you open the phone to the bigger inner screen. The crease on my Fold 8 Ultra is hardly noticeable. I can barely feel it or see it unless light hits it at just an angle. As of writing this review I've owned the Fold 8 Ultra for a little over a month now and this has remained true. We'll see if the crease remains this unnoticeable in time. Another thing is the battery. I can get away with two days on a single charge if I use the phone normally. If I use it a bit more heavily I can get by on one charge for the entire day. In addition, should I need to charge the phone pronto it can be fast charged with 45 watt charging. I charge mine with my fold 5's charger, which is a 25 watt charger. It is plenty. Besides all that it is a gorgeous looking phone. It looks sharp and elegant from a glance. I get many questions about it - even from people that have seen me with a Fold 5. Not that getting attention is important for a phone, but it is as it is. In total, a great phone.

top_reviews.title: The best foldable. Excellent smartphone + mini tablet in one
top_reviews.variant: Color: Violet Shadow Size: 512GB Style: Fold8 Ultra Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: Went from Fold 3 to Fold 8. Firstly, this fold pretty much fixed any issue I had with foldables. Thin Lightweight Good Battery Quick charging Good Camera Less crease Inner display is bright outdoors for viewing. With phone closed, you can use front display as a smartphone normally. It unfolds into a mini tablet experience. Phone is durable and feels good in hands. Software is very good and everything works well for android, minus a few quirks. Lots of features to try out and customize. Main complaint is now camera bump (phone does not lay flat). And the selfie camera holes. This is simply the best foldable. Easily the best phone. And most portable mini tablet ever. Samsungs finest thus far.

top_reviews.title: Love the foldable design
top_reviews.variant: Color: Graphite Size: 256GB Style: Fold8 Ultra Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: I really like the foldable screen. It’s convenient for multitasking and watching videos, and the camera takes clear photos. Overall, I’m happy with it.

top_reviews.title: Best foldable on the international market.
top_reviews.variant: Color: Violet Shadow Size: 512GB Style: Fold8 Ultra Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: The phone has exceeded my expectations and has been nothing but a treat, I've been using it everyday non stop, the crease is as good as the oppo find n6 as well as processing power. The camera quality isn't a major upgrade for me as I cam from the S-- Ultra series but the outcomes of the pics I've took so far are more than exceptional, especially with one ui 9 and the enhanced AI features and capabilities. I would definitely recommend this phone, I am a little sad about no pen support but after a few days of use for work and personal, the pen didn't become something I would have required, the 8 inch inner display is enough.

top_reviews.title: Buy it!
top_reviews.variant: Color: Violet Shadow Size: 512GB Style: Fold8 Ultra Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: This is the best phone I've ever used. I love how thin it is and it's a slim phone when closed and can open to a tablet when needed. Paired mine with a Rokform case and it's perfect. This is my first foldable and don't think I'll be going back to a traditional phone slab. Little pricey but from what you get I think its worth the bundle you get in one form factor.

top_reviews.title: If you have the disposable funds and you really want a foldable...this is for you!
top_reviews.variant: Color: Violet Shadow Size: 512GB Style: Fold8 Ultra Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: Good unit albeit an expensive one. If this is the first purchase of a foldable android that has the normal dimensions of a mainstream bar type cell phone, this Samsung is quite good, bright screen, easier to open, crease in the middle is minimal, screen is not highly reflective, good battery, powerful unit. I own a Fold 7 and although the Fold 8 Ultra is better in the areas aforementioned, it is not so much better that one needs to spend over $2K on a replacement a year later. These devices still need babysitting because they are highly subject to damage form dust and water which compromises durability. However, if money is not an issue this device is a prime device in its class in this country. I am not going to cover the technical specifications because most buyers are hardly likely to utilize the device beyond it's primary functions and those are the ones most obvious that I have mentioned. If I did not own the Fold 7, I would probably have kept the unit but I returned the 8, not because it was not a great and attractive device but because it was not a $1000 better than the device I have and the trade in value of my less than 1 year old device was 50% depreciation which was unreasonable. The Fold 8 Ultra is a nice device but I am not sure that it is really worth the cost...Amazon's offering is outstanding with the gift card so if the offer is still available and you really want the device the Amazon offer is WAYYY better than Samsung's which is really them upselling another device simultaneously. Good luck if you decide you have the disposable income to spend it on this device. Not 5 stars on the rating because of the cost...one other thing...there is still a crease in the middle of the unfolded screen just in case you are wondering.

top_reviews.title: A great phone, though pricey
top_reviews.variant: Color: Graphite Size: 512GB Style: Fold8 Ultra Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: The Fold 8 Ultra isn't my first foldable phone. My first is its older sibling, the Fold 5. The Fold 5 was a great phone in many ways. The Fold 8 Ultra improved on the Fold 5 in many ways. The chief thing is that it is a light phone. Another thing is that when folded it feels like a normal phone. It is perhaps very slightly thicker than a typical slate phone. We're talking about mm thicker, tops. The magic happens when you open the phone to the bigger inner screen. The crease on my Fold 8 Ultra is hardly noticeable. I can barely feel it or see it unless light hits it at just an angle. As of writing this review I've owned the Fold 8 Ultra for a little over a month now and this has remained true. We'll see if the crease remains this unnoticeable in time. Another thing is the battery. I can get away with two days on a single charge if I use the phone normally. If I use it a bit more heavily I can get by on one charge for the entire day. In addition, should I need to charge the phone pronto it can be fast charged with 45 watt charging. I charge mine with my fold 5's charger, which is a 25 watt charger. It is plenty. Besides all that it is a gorgeous looking phone. It looks sharp and elegant from a glance. I get many questions about it - even from people that have seen me with a Fold 5. Not that getting attention is important for a phone, but it is as it is. In total, a great phone.

It unfolds into a mini tablet experience. Phone is durable and feels good in hands. Software is very good and everything works well for android, minus a few quirks. Lots of features to try out and customize. Main complaint is now camera bump (phone does not lay flat). And the selfie camera holes. This is simply the best foldable. Easily the best phone. top_reviews.title: My Honest Take on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 (First Fold, First Impressions... and Now I'm Sold)
top_reviews.variant: Color: Graphite Size: 512GB Style: Fold8 Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: I'll be upfront, I went into this hesitant coming from an iPhone 15 Pro and an S26 Ultra. This is my first foldable, and I had all the usual doubts durability, hinge wear, whether it would actually hold up as a daily driver or just end up as an expensive novelty that would be returned. A few weeks in, I can say I was wrong to worry. This thing has earned a permanent spot as my main device. What I Actually Use It For My day-to-day isn't crazy and consists of phone calls, texting, a lot of streaming (MLB, YouTube, Netflix, Disney+), web browsing, online shopping, general entertainment, and now schoolwork for my college courses utilizing DeX, however I don't use it for gaming. The Fold 8 handles all of it without breaking a sweat, and honestly, it's doing more than I expected going in. Battery life has been solid and I get plenty of juice to get me through the day. Performance For everything I throw at it, performance has been smooth. Streaming looks great on the bigger canvas, browsing is snappy, and switching between apps for coursework has been painless. I haven't run into any slowdown that made me question the hardware. This could be a different story 6-12-24 months from now, but right now this thing is snappy and smooth. One thing I cannot forget to mention is the speakers. For some the speakers will be an issue. They're on one side of the screen unfolded and it creates an off balance listening experience. This however does not bother me in particular. The more you use it the more you get used to it and if you're someone who uses headphones a lot then you really wont notice. Heat This was my biggest concern after seeing a lot of Youtube videos mention this. For me I have no overheating issues to report, with one exception. Like any phone initial setup it ran a little warm, which seems to be common with these devices during the first sync and data transfer. Since then, it's been business as usual, even during longer streaming sessions. Also to be fair, I'm not a gamer so I cannot speak to playing any games on his either. Size and Feel The screen size strikes a great balance. The front display is small enought to handle the texting and quick glance notifications, but the inner screen is big enough to actually enjoy videos and reading. Not to mention the phone itself is light and comfortable to hold, even unfolded. It doesn't feel like a brick, and it doesn't feel fragile either. It's genuinely a delight to use, which surprised me for a first foldable. For those that remember it does give a little bit of that Blackberry vibe when folded and an iPad Mini vibe when unfolded for frame of reference. The Case Situation This is really my only complaint, and it's more about timing than the phone itself. Since it's early in its release cycle, decent case options are still catching up. If you're picky about protection and style, be patient. This will improve as more accessory makers get on board. This form factor feels like it has real staying power. With foldables maturing and rumors swirling about Apple entering the space with an iPhone Ultra, I think Samsung's Fold line is positioned to be a serious competitor rather than a niche product. If my experience is any indication, this is the direction phones are heading, and Samsung has a real head start. Bottom Line I went into this skeptical and was even really nervous the first few days but came out impressed. If you've been on the fence about a first foldable, the Z Fold 8 is a strong argument to jump in.

top_reviews.title: My Honest Take on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 (First Fold, First Impressions... and Now I'm Sold)
top_reviews.variant: Color: Graphite Size: 512GB Style: Fold8 Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: I'll be upfront, I went into this hesitant coming from an iPhone 15 Pro and an S26 Ultra. This is my first foldable, and I had all the usual doubts durability, hinge wear, whether it would actually hold up as a daily driver or just end up as an expensive novelty that would be returned. A few weeks in, I can say I was wrong to worry. This thing has earned a permanent spot as my main device. What I Actually Use It For My day-to-day isn't crazy and consists of phone calls, texting, a lot of streaming (MLB, YouTube, Netflix, Disney+), web browsing, online shopping, general entertainment, and now schoolwork for my college courses utilizing DeX, however I don't use it for gaming. The Fold 8 handles all of it without breaking a sweat, and honestly, it's doing more than I expected going in. Battery life has been solid and I get plenty of juice to get me through the day. Performance For everything I throw at it, performance has been smooth. Streaming looks great on the bigger canvas, browsing is snappy, and switching between apps for coursework has been painless. I haven't run into any slowdown that made me question the hardware. This could be a different story 6-12-24 months from now, but right now this thing is snappy and smooth. One thing I cannot forget to mention is the speakers. For some the speakers will be an issue. They're on one side of the screen unfolded and it creates an off balance listening experience. This however does not bother me in particular. The more you use it the more you get used to it and if you're someone who uses headphones a lot then you really wont notice. Heat This was my biggest concern after seeing a lot of Youtube videos mention this. For me I have no overheating issues to report, with one exception. Like any phone initial setup it ran a little warm, which seems to be common with these devices during the first sync and data transfer. Since then, it's been business as usual, even during longer streaming sessions. Also to be fair, I'm not a gamer so I cannot speak to playing any games on his either. Size and Feel The screen size strikes a great balance. The front display is small enought to handle the texting and quick glance notifications, but the inner screen is big enough to actually enjoy videos and reading. Not to mention the phone itself is light and comfortable to hold, even unfolded. It doesn't feel like a brick, and it doesn't feel fragile either. It's genuinely a delight to use, which surprised me for a first foldable. For those that remember it does give a little bit of that Blackberry vibe when folded and an iPad Mini vibe when unfolded for frame of reference. The Case Situation This is really my only complaint, and it's more about timing than the phone itself. Since it's early in its release cycle, decent case options are still catching up. If you're picky about protection and style, be patient. This will improve as more accessory makers get on board. This form factor feels like it has real staying power. With foldables maturing and rumors swirling about Apple entering the space with an iPhone Ultra, I think Samsung's Fold line is positioned to be a serious competitor rather than a niche product. If my experience is any indication, this is the direction phones are heading, and Samsung has a real head start. Bottom Line I went into this skeptical and was even really nervous the first few days but came out impressed. If you've been on the fence about a first foldable, the Z Fold 8 is a strong argument to jump in.

top_reviews.title: In love with this

top_reviews.body: Such a great phone. Battery life has been solid. I love using both screens, and the smaller/wider size is a treat to use day to day. Cameras work well, though not pixel quality. Color is awesome. Still getting used to OneUI, but I havent had any app issues with the form factor so far, everything works. Mine is in a case, but the included free screen protector replacement is a nice detail. Its quite expensive, but if you will use the features and eliminate a tablet, likely worth it over several years.

top_reviews.title: My new bestie
top_reviews.variant: Color: Lavender Size: 256GB Style: Fold8 Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: My new Z Fold8 is amazing! I absolutely love how easily it fits in my pocket while still giving me such a large screen when I open it. The bigger screen is perfect for watching movies, multitasking, and getting things done. The battery also holds a charge really well. My phone fell and not one Crack, the color is pretty, and so easy to use as a set up. I’m very happy with my purchase and love this phone!

top_reviews.title: First Foldable - Awesome so far
top_reviews.variant: Color: Graphite Size: 256GB Style: Fold8 Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: I jumped ship from an iPhone 15 Pro Max and the experience has been good so far. Getting to relearn android after so many years away has been tricky but manageable. Samsung Smart Switch made it relatively easy to transfer all the data over to the Fold 8. The form factor is awesome and once you get used to the cover screen, it makes other Max/Ultra phones seem unnecessarily ginormous. The light weight is also a huge plus since it is lighter than my previous iPhone and is essentially both a phone and a tablet.

top_reviews.title: Great phone!
top_reviews.variant: Color: Lavender Size: 512GB Style: Fold8 Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: I finally took the plunge and moved to a foldable and I absolutely LOVE it. Hands down one of my all time favorite phones. Samsung always delivers quality, but I do think new phones are becoming a bit overpriced these days. The crease is still barely visible after a month of regular use, so it seems pretty durable. I love how easy it us to use when closed as well. Its super easy to maneuver with one hand which makes texting so much better. Overall I am very happy with my purchase.

top_reviews.title: The new design is a game changer!
top_reviews.variant: Color: Graphite Size: 256GB Style: Fold8 Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: The new wide design is much better! It's a replacement for my old Fold 4 which is outdated. Build quality is excellent and much lighter. Battery life is much better and Software works seamlessly. Transferring my old phone was easy and took less than 20 minutes at my Wireless Store. Overall I'd have to say it's a Great Phone!

top_reviews.title: Fold 8 is great. Amazon pre order is not.
top_reviews.variant: Color: Graphite Size: 256GB Style: Fold8 Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: Fold 8 has been a wonderful device. Absolutely the best folding phone I have ever used. The only major con is the cameras aren't great so if you are into pro level photos maybe look at another phone(however photos taken look amazing on the inner display). Not the perfect device but overall it's a really nice and innovative phone. Now a PSA. The pre order experience with Amazon was awful...... I pre ordered 10 days before launch and got my phone about a month after launch. I called Amazon customer service to see if I could adjust my pre order from the 256 to 512 since it was in stock about 1 week after launch and customer service said I'd have to cancel my pre order lose all the bonuses(which were good) and just re buy it. Customer service was terrible and unable to help in any way. If it weren't for the bonuses I wouldn't use Amazon to pre order a phone.

top_reviews.title: My Honest Take on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 (First Fold, First Impressions... and Now I'm Sold)
top_reviews.variant: Color: Graphite Size: 512GB Style: Fold8 Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: I'll be upfront, I went into this hesitant coming from an iPhone 15 Pro and an S26 Ultra. This is my first foldable, and I had all the usual doubts durability, hinge wear, whether it would actually hold up as a daily driver or just end up as an expensive novelty that would be returned. A few weeks in, I can say I was wrong to worry. This thing has earned a permanent spot as my main device. What I Actually Use It For My day-to-day isn't crazy and consists of phone calls, texting, a lot of streaming (MLB, YouTube, Netflix, Disney+), web browsing, online shopping, general entertainment, and now schoolwork for my college courses utilizing DeX, however I don't use it for gaming. The Fold 8 handles all of it without breaking a sweat, and honestly, it's doing more than I expected going in. Battery life has been solid and I get plenty of juice to get me through the day. Performance For everything I throw at it, performance has been smooth. Streaming looks great on the bigger canvas, browsing is snappy, and switching between apps for coursework has been painless. I haven't run into any slowdown that made me question the hardware. This could be a different story 6-12-24 months from now, but right now this thing is snappy and smooth. One thing I cannot forget to mention is the speakers. For some the speakers will be an issue. They're on one side of the screen unfolded and it creates an off balance listening experience. This however does not bother me in particular. The more you use it the more you get used to it and if you're someone who uses headphones a lot then you really wont notice. Heat This was my biggest concern after seeing a lot of Youtube videos mention this. For me I have no overheating issues to report, with one exception. Like any phone initial setup it ran a little warm, which seems to be common with these devices during the first sync and data transfer. Since then, it's been business as usual, even during longer streaming sessions. Also to be fair, I'm not a gamer so I cannot speak to playing any games on his either. Size and Feel The screen size strikes a great balance. The front display is small enought to handle the texting and quick glance notifications, but the inner screen is big enough to actually enjoy videos and reading. Not to mention the phone itself is light and comfortable to hold, even unfolded. It doesn't feel like a brick, and it doesn't feel fragile either. It's genuinely a delight to use, which surprised me for a first foldable. For those that remember it does give a little bit of that Blackberry vibe when folded and an iPad Mini vibe when unfolded for frame of reference. The Case Situation This is really my only complaint, and it's more about timing than the phone itself. Since it's early in its release cycle, decent case options are still catching up. If you're picky about protection and style, be patient. This will improve as more accessory makers get on board. This form factor feels like it has real staying power. With foldables maturing and rumors swirling about Apple entering the space with an iPhone Ultra, I think Samsung's Fold line is positioned to be a serious competitor rather than a niche product. If my experience is any indication, this is the direction phones are heading, and Samsung has a real head start. Bottom Line I went into this skeptical and was even really nervous the first few days but came out impressed. If you've been on the fence about a first foldable, the Z Fold 8 is a strong argument to jump in.

top_reviews.title: My Honest Take on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 (First Fold, First Impressions... and Now I'm Sold)
top_reviews.variant: Color: Graphite Size: 512GB Style: Fold8 Pattern Name: Phone
top_reviews.body: I'll be upfront, I went into this hesitant coming from an iPhone 15 Pro and an S26 Ultra. This is my first foldable, and I had all the usual doubts durability, hinge wear, whether it would actually hold up as a daily driver or just end up as an expensive novelty that would be returned. A few weeks in, I can say I was wrong to worry. This thing has earned a permanent spot as my main device. What I Actually Use It For My day-to-day isn't crazy and consists of phone calls, texting, a lot of streaming (MLB, YouTube, Netflix, Disney+), web browsing, online shopping, general entertainment, and now schoolwork for my college courses utilizing DeX, however I don't use it for gaming. The Fold 8 handles all of it without breaking a sweat, and honestly, it's doing more than I expected going in. Battery life has been solid and I get plenty of juice to get me through the day. Performance For everything I throw at it, performance has been smooth. Streaming looks great on the bigger canvas, browsing is snappy, and switching between apps for coursework has been painless. I haven't run into any slowdown that made me question the hardware. This could be a different story 6-12-24 months from now, but right now this thing is snappy and smooth. One thing I cannot forget to mention is the speakers. For some the speakers will be an issue. They're on one side of the screen unfolded and it creates an off balance listening experience. This however does not bother me in particular. The more you use it the more you get used to it and if you're someone who uses headphones a lot then you really wont notice. Heat This was my biggest concern after seeing a lot of Youtube videos mention this. For me I have no overheating issues to report, with one exception. Like any phone initial setup it ran a little warm, which seems to be common with these devices during the first sync and data transfer. Since then, it's been business as usual, even during longer streaming sessions. Also to be fair, I'm not a gamer so I cannot speak to playing any games on his either. Size and Feel The screen size strikes a great balance. The front display is small enought to handle the texting and quick glance notifications, but the inner screen is big enough to actually enjoy videos and reading. Not to mention the phone itself is light and comfortable to hold, even unfolded. It doesn't feel like a brick, and it doesn't feel fragile either. It's genuinely a delight to use, which surprised me for a first foldable. For those that remember it does give a little bit of that Blackberry vibe when folded and an iPad Mini vibe when unfolded for frame of reference. The Case Situation This is really my only complaint, and it's more about timing than the phone itself. Since it's early in its release cycle, decent case options are still catching up. If you're picky about protection and style, be patient. This will improve as more accessory makers get on board. This form factor feels like it has real staying power. With foldables maturing and rumors swirling about Apple entering the space with an iPhone Ultra, I think Samsung's Fold line is positioned to be a serious competitor rather than a niche product. If my experience is any indication, this is the direction phones are heading, and Samsung has a real head start. Bottom Line I went into this skeptical and was even really nervous the first few days but came out impressed. If you've been on the fence about a first foldable, the Z Fold 8 is a strong argument to jump in.

What are the key features of Galaxy Z Flip8?
Galaxy Z Flip8 delivers a lightweight, foldable experience. It is our lightest and thinnest Flip ever at 180 grams and 6.1 millimeters. The lightweight design means you can carry it comfortably in your hand or pocket throughout the day.
What is the difference between Galaxy Z Flip7 and Galaxy Z Flip8?
If you value a slim, foldable design, the Galaxy Flip8 is a compelling upgrade choice. It is 8 grams lighter than the Galaxy Flip7 and featurees and elevated camera system thanks to tools like Photo Assist, Super Steady and Flip Shot.
I’m switching to Galaxy for the first time. How easy is it?
The excitement of finding your perfect foldable phone can also bring up anxiety about making the switch from iPhone. Bring over photos, contacts and passwords. Share files and encrypt messages in a way you’re used to. And do it all on Galaxy Z Flip8.
How durable is Galaxy Z Flip8?
Galaxy Z Flip8 is fortified with materials that strengthen the device for long-lasting durability. The Armor Aluminum frame provides enhanced protection for the device's internal components and exterior edges without adding excessive bulk.
Can I customize Galaxy Flip8's cover screen?
Yes you can customize Galaxy Flip8's cover screen to match your style and do more without having to unfold the device. You can also view your personalized insights directly on FlexWindow with Now Brief.

top_reviews.title: Great Upgrade from Galaxy Watch 5
top_reviews.variant: Color: Cream Size: 40mm Style: Bluetooth Pattern Name: Watch9 Only
top_reviews.body: As someone who loved her Galaxy Watch 5, I was very excited to finally upgrade to the Watch 9. My old watch finally died this week, which seemed like perfect timing with the new coming out (though I wish I could have taken advantage of pre-order deals but alas). Luckily, I was able to get a replacement pretty quickly and in a color I liked as well. First, I have to say that while I love my watch, it was a bit of a panic attack at first, as the setup was way different from my first watch. As someone who mostly used her watch for productivity tasks, step tracking, and heart rate monitoring during workouts, I found all the new fitness-tracking features extremely overwhelming. I almost sent it back because I wasn't sure if I wanted all these options. Since I didn't want to put up with the lack of functionality and durability of the Fitbit, I decided to stick it out and just turn off some of the features. It was better to have them in case I wanted them later. Once I got my watch working, though, I was very impressed. The fit has been great and it seems more durable than my old watch. The only disappointing thing about it has been that it doesn't work with any of my old Galaxy Watch chargers, which is annoying since I will have to buy new ones. Fairly minor, but still disappointing. I also love that there are so many band options (I personally am not a fan of silicone bands). Overall though, I love the color of my watch and how it feels, and consider it a good value for the money.

top_reviews.title: Outstanding!
top_reviews.variant: Color: Graphite Size: 40mm Style: Cellular Pattern Name: Watch9 Only
top_reviews.body: I bought this watch for my mom. She's 85 years old and has fallen a couple of times. She doesn't always carry her phone, which would enable her to call for help. This watch is a GREAT idea! I was able to put it on our phone carrier network (Patriot Mobile) very easily. Her phone is connected via Bluetooth to her phone, and it also has its own LTE data. So, if she happens to be away from her phone, she can still call for help. The watch is equipped with a fall detection function. It will automatically connect her to someone who can call 9/11 for her. She can make and answer calls just like a phone. It has so many other fantastic functions. I'm happy to say that it is user-friendly; probably one of the greatest features since Mom is 85. You can adjust the font size for better readability. It's durable and nice-looking. I actually purchased some stretchy nylon fabric bands so she is able to put in and remove it more easily than with the band it comes with. The 40mm is plenty large enough. The 44mm would be huge on her wrist. Definitely a worthwhile purchase!

top_reviews.body: I'm really enjoying this watch. I have small wrists, so this 40 mm works the best. The larger face dial would have been overpowering my wrists and heavier. The only thing I wasn't crazy about is the wristband I ended up ordering a different kind that is magnetic and works best for my wrists.

top_reviews.title: Excellent choice Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 40mm
top_reviews.variant: Color: Cream Size: 40mm Style: Cellular Pattern Name: Watch9 Only
top_reviews.body: I really like the Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 (40mm) but, the only complaint I have is the battery life. I thought the battery would last longer. I had a Samsung Galaxy Watch5 Pro pror to purchasing SG watch 9. The Watch 9 is great. A lot of updated features, such as the improved Samsung Health.

top_reviews.title: Not Recommended. Wait for Galaxy Watch 10 or 11 LTE or get Watch 8 LTE.
top_reviews.variant: Color: Silver Size: 44mm Style: Cellular Pattern Name: Watch9 Only
top_reviews.body: Not recommended! I've had to change my opinion of the Galaxy Watch 9 LTE after some time with it. Best to wait for the Watch 10 or 11 LTE for hopefully a much bigger silicon-carbon battery and several other needed changes. The latest round is discovering Samsung apparently started selling these watches without the ability to buy spare charging pucks anywhere retail! The existing puck for Galaxy Watch 5/6/7 (and maybe 8? can't confirm) does NOT work with Watch 9 LTE. Comes up with a yellow triangle "incompatible charger" symbol. After time speaking on the phone with Samsung Customer Service I was able to order what is supposed to be one through Samsung Parts, run by Encompass (part# GH96-17240A). Having spare car & office pucks for a watch with a battery that only lasts for a day is crucial. I have two spare pucks for my old Galaxy Watch 5 Pro for that reason. UPDATE 9/23/26! THIS JUST GOT WORSE. No word on the Watch 9 charging puck order, so I called Samsung Parts for status to learn it is now BACKORDERED UNTIL 11/14/26 and worse they say that is just an estimate, could be longer. :( Two MONTHS from when I placed the order for something that should have been available when the watch came out. :( Wow. The alarm volume on the Watch 9 has turned out to be so soft I can barely hear it. I've had to go back to my old Watch 5 Pro for timing the yard sprinklers and such. I can hear that one in the next room. The "M/L" watch band is woefully short, as many others have posted now. It should be a "M". Samsung needs to make an "L" available and ideally an "XL". The band can be replaced for some other brand, but it is the principle of the thing. For $450, a large company like Samsung should have a properly sized watch bands available to ship with the watch. The Watch 5 Pro band has the same problem. Nothing screams "excess profit" like this issue, IMHO. :( The battery life is a joke, as many people have posted, lasting around 24 hours when many other watches will go for days. The battery life in my old Watch 5 Pro is even less, about 18 hours, so I figured that I would get used to it, but hasn't happened. Especially irritating knowing silicon carbon batteries with much greater capacity are out there. One of the reasons I hung on to my old Galaxy 5 Pro for so long is that the glass display is completely surrounded by round metal and therefore chip-proof. Well sure enough this display already has an edge chip on it. :( The Watch 9 does have a few good things still. I bought it to get LTE so I could make an emergency phone call if the phone isn't around. That still works via the Spectrum Mobile $11/month watch add-on plan. The Wi-Fi and Bluetooth versions are updated from the Watch 5 Pro and work better. And the biggee: the aluminum Watch 9 is light enough to wear all day long where the titanium Watch 5 Pro wasn't, without becoming annoying. But even then the Watch 9 LTE is 80% the same as the Watch 8 LTE! The case size, display, memory, and bio-sensors are all the same. Might was well get a cheaper (used, even) Watch 8 LTE to carry over to the watch 10 or 11. I'll be looking forward to trading-in this Watch 9 LTE the minute Samsung comes up with a bigger-battery LTE watch that will go a minimum of 2 days on a charge. Also looking for Watch 10 or 11 to have 5G rather than just LTE, Wi-Fi 7 & 6GHz vs. just Wi-Fi 6, and satellite communication - which the Snapdragon Wear Elite chip in it already supports. C'mon Samsung, time to step up your game here. :(

top_reviews.body: As someone who loved her Galaxy Watch 5, I was very excited to finally upgrade to the Watch 9. My old watch finally died this week, which seemed like perfect timing with the new coming out (though I wish I could have taken advantage of pre-order deals but alas). Luckily, I was able to get a replacement pretty quickly and in a color I liked as well. First, I have to say that while I love my watch, it was a bit of a panic attack at first, as the setup was way different from my first watch. As someone who mostly used her watch for productivity tasks, step tracking, and heart rate monitoring during workouts, I found all the new fitness-tracking features extremely overwhelming. I almost sent it back because I wasn't sure if I wanted all these options. Since I didn't want to put up with the lack of functionality and durability of the Fitbit, I decided to stick it out and just turn off some of the features. It was better to have them in case I wanted them later. Once I got my watch working, though, I was very impressed. The fit has been great and it seems more durable than my old watch. The only disappointing thing about it has been that it doesn't work with any of my old Galaxy Watch chargers, which is annoying since I will have to buy new ones. Fairly minor, but still disappointing. I also love that there are so many band options (I personally am not a fan of silicone bands). Overall though, I love the color of my watch and how it feels, and consider it a good value for the money.

top_reviews.title: Outstanding!
top_reviews.variant: Color: Graphite Size: 40mm Style: Cellular Pattern Name: Watch9 Only
top_reviews.body: I bought this watch for my mom. She's 85 years old and has fallen a couple of times. She doesn't always carry her phone, which would enable her to call for help. This watch is a GREAT idea! I was able to put it on our phone carrier network (Patriot Mobile) very easily. Her phone is connected via Bluetooth to her phone, and it also has its own LTE data. So, if she happens to be away from her phone, she can still call for help. The watch is equipped with a fall detection function. It will automatically connect her to someone who can call 9/11 for her. She can make and answer calls just like a phone. It has so many other fantastic functions. I'm happy to say that it is user-friendly; probably one of the greatest features since Mom is 85. You can adjust the font size for better readability. It's durable and nice-looking. I actually purchased some stretchy nylon fabric bands so she is able to put in and remove it more easily than with the band it comes with. The 40mm is plenty large enough. The 44mm would be huge on her wrist. Definitely a worthwhile purchase!

top_reviews.title: Not Recommended. Wait for Galaxy Watch 10 or 11 LTE or get Watch 8 LTE.
top_reviews.variant: Color: Silver Size: 44mm Style: Cellular Pattern Name: Watch9 Only
top_reviews.body: Not recommended! I've had to change my opinion of the Galaxy Watch 9 LTE after some time with it. Best to wait for the Watch 10 or 11 LTE for hopefully a much bigger silicon-carbon battery and several other needed changes. The latest round is discovering Samsung apparently started selling these watches without the ability to buy spare charging pucks anywhere retail! The existing puck for Galaxy Watch 5/6/7 (and maybe 8? can't confirm) does NOT work with Watch 9 LTE. Comes up with a yellow triangle "incompatible charger" symbol. After time speaking on the phone with Samsung Customer Service I was able to order what is supposed to be one through Samsung Parts, run by Encompass (part# GH96-17240A). Having spare car & office pucks for a watch with a battery that only lasts for a day is crucial. I have two spare pucks for my old Galaxy Watch 5 Pro for that reason. UPDATE 9/23/26! THIS JUST GOT WORSE. No word on the Watch 9 charging puck order, so I called Samsung Parts for status to learn it is now BACKORDERED UNTIL 11/14/26 and worse they say that is just an estimate, could be longer. :( Two MONTHS from when I placed the order for something that should have been available when the watch came out. :( Wow. The alarm volume on the Watch 9 has turned out to be so soft I can barely hear it. I've had to go back to my old Watch 5 Pro for timing the yard sprinklers and such. I can hear that one in the next room. The "M/L" watch band is woefully short, as many others have posted now. It should be a "M". Samsung needs to make an "L" available and ideally an "XL". The band can be replaced for some other brand, but it is the principle of the thing. For $450, a large company like Samsung should have a properly sized watch bands available to ship with the watch. The Watch 5 Pro band has the same problem. Nothing screams "excess profit" like this issue, IMHO. :( The battery life is a joke, as many people have posted, lasting around 24 hours when many other watches will go for days. The battery life in my old Watch 5 Pro is even less, about 18 hours, so I figured that I would get used to it, but hasn't happened. Especially irritating knowing silicon carbon batteries with much greater capacity are out there. One of the reasons I hung on to my old Galaxy 5 Pro for so long is that the glass display is completely surrounded by round metal and therefore chip-proof. Well sure enough this display already has an edge chip on it. :( The Watch 9 does have a few good things still. I bought it to get LTE so I could make an emergency phone call if the phone isn't around. That still works via the Spectrum Mobile $11/month watch add-on plan. The Wi-Fi and Bluetooth versions are updated from the Watch 5 Pro and work better. And the biggee: the aluminum Watch 9 is light enough to wear all day long where the titanium Watch 5 Pro wasn't, without becoming annoying. But even then the Watch 9 LTE is 80% the same as the Watch 8 LTE! The case size, display, memory, and bio-sensors are all the same. Might was well get a cheaper (used, even) Watch 8 LTE to carry over to the watch 10 or 11. I'll be looking forward to trading-in this Watch 9 LTE the minute Samsung comes up with a bigger-battery LTE watch that will go a minimum of 2 days on a charge. Also looking for Watch 10 or 11 to have 5G rather than just LTE, Wi-Fi 7 & 6GHz vs. just Wi-Fi 6, and satellite communication - which the Snapdragon Wear Elite chip in it already supports. C'mon Samsung, time to step up your game here. :(

top_reviews.variant: Color: Graphite Size: 40mm Style: Bluetooth Pattern Name: Watch9 Only
top_reviews.body: Perfect watch face size for an average womans wrist size, but the band with the 40mm watch is very small, i could only use it with the last hole and it was tight. I bought the bluetooth version for the health tracking features which I love so far but am still getting used to them. I noticed once I turned the health tracking features on the battery runs down faster. I probably went from charging every 1.5-2 days to once a day and that is with the AOD off. For example, I had it charged to 100% around 9:00 am, and with normal activity throughout the day it is now at 52% at 6:55 pm. Fast response times; great health tracking features with vitals, sleep tracking, automatic workout detection; and it had a bright clear display. I just wish the battery lasted a tad longer.

top_reviews.title: Light and low profile.
top_reviews.variant: Color: Graphite Size: 40mm Style: Bluetooth Pattern Name: Watch9 Only
top_reviews.body: Super light weight. Best smartwatch I've owned. Only issue is battery life is rather short. It does charge rather quick so it evens out.

top_reviews.title: Good Buy
top_reviews.variant: Color: Cream Size: 40mm Style: Bluetooth Pattern Name: Watch9 Only
top_reviews.body: Love the watch. I don't love the battery life. Have to charge daily.

top_reviews.title: Great Upgrade from Galaxy Watch 5
top_reviews.variant: Color: Cream Size: 40mm Style: Bluetooth Pattern Name: Watch9 Only
top_reviews.body: As someone who loved her Galaxy Watch 5, I was very excited to finally upgrade to the Watch 9. My old watch finally died this week, which seemed like perfect timing with the new coming out (though I wish I could have taken advantage of pre-order deals but alas). Luckily, I was able to get a replacement pretty quickly and in a color I liked as well. First, I have to say that while I love my watch, it was a bit of a panic attack at first, as the setup was way different from my first watch. As someone who mostly used her watch for productivity tasks, step tracking, and heart rate monitoring during workouts, I found all the new fitness-tracking features extremely overwhelming. I almost sent it back because I wasn't sure if I wanted all these options. Since I didn't want to put up with the lack of functionality and durability of the Fitbit, I decided to stick it out and just turn off some of the features. It was better to have them in case I wanted them later. Once I got my watch working, though, I was very impressed. The fit has been great and it seems more durable than my old watch. The only disappointing thing about it has been that it doesn't work with any of my old Galaxy Watch chargers, which is annoying since I will have to buy new ones. Fairly minor, but still disappointing. I also love that there are so many band options (I personally am not a fan of silicone bands). Overall though, I love the color of my watch and how it feels, and consider it a good value for the money.

top_reviews.title: I like the watch
top_reviews.variant: Color: Cream Size: 40mm Style: Bluetooth Pattern Name: Watch9 Only
top_reviews.body: The watch itself arrived in perfect condition and so far i like it! I wasnt a big fan of square circle ish form factor like this one till i got mine, now that im using it i feel like this new form factor is actually not that bad. I literally just upgraded my watch from galaxy watch 6 to 9 and duhh the upgrades are significant. Its fluid and has many new features. The only downside is the charging speed. It takes 2 hours is to get it full which is way slower compared to my watch 6 that only takes ~1 hour. But fortunately the battery life is good. And also the strap is really short but still usable. Is it worth the money? Well i got myself a 50$ amazon gift card so the value of the watch itself was only ~329 bucks, for someone who just upgraded from watch 6 this is way to go but if you have watch 7 or 8, i wont suggest you to get this watch.

top_reviews.title: Great new functions!
top_reviews.variant: Color: Graphite Size: 40mm Style: Bluetooth Pattern Name: Watch9 Only
top_reviews.body: I've been very happy with this model compared to my original galaxy watch 8 and it was well worth the money for the upgraded functions! I've had zero connectivity issues with the watch and every feature has worked perfect for my health tracking needs. The size I chose fit perfect for me and has been very enjoyable to use overall! I will say the biggest reason for the upgrade was the new features which compile information much better than previous models and present it in a more easy to read manner! I'll gladly stick with samsung watchs because of usability and durability compared to other brands!

top_reviews.title: Outstanding!
top_reviews.variant: Color: Graphite Size: 40mm Style: Cellular Pattern Name: Watch9 Only
top_reviews.body: I bought this watch for my mom. She's 85 years old and has fallen a couple of times. She doesn't always carry her phone, which would enable her to call for help. This watch is a GREAT idea! I was able to put it on our phone carrier network (Patriot Mobile) very easily. Her phone is connected via Bluetooth to her phone, and it also has its own LTE data. So, if she happens to be away from her phone, she can still call for help. The watch is equipped with a fall detection function. It will automatically connect her to someone who can call 9/11 for her. She can make and answer calls just like a phone. It has so many other fantastic functions. I'm happy to say that it is user-friendly; probably one of the greatest features since Mom is 85. You can adjust the font size for better readability. It's durable and nice-looking. I actually purchased some stretchy nylon fabric bands so she is able to put in and remove it more easily than with the band it comes with. The 40mm is plenty large enough. The 44mm would be huge on her wrist. Definitely a worthwhile purchase!

top_reviews.body: I'm really enjoying this watch. I have small wrists, so this 40 mm works the best. The larger face dial would have been overpowering my wrists and heavier. The only thing I wasn't crazy about is the wristband I ended up ordering a different kind that is magnetic and works best for my wrists.

top_reviews.title: Excellent choice Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 40mm
top_reviews.variant: Color: Cream Size: 40mm Style: Cellular Pattern Name: Watch9 Only
top_reviews.body: I really like the Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 (40mm) but, the only complaint I have is the battery life. I thought the battery would last longer. I had a Samsung Galaxy Watch5 Pro pror to purchasing SG watch 9. The Watch 9 is great. A lot of updated features, such as the improved Samsung Health.

top_reviews.title: Not Recommended. Wait for Galaxy Watch 10 or 11 LTE or get Watch 8 LTE.
top_reviews.variant: Color: Silver Size: 44mm Style: Cellular Pattern Name: Watch9 Only
top_reviews.body: Not recommended! I've had to change my opinion of the Galaxy Watch 9 LTE after some time with it. Best to wait for the Watch 10 or 11 LTE for hopefully a much bigger silicon-carbon battery and several other needed changes. The latest round is discovering Samsung apparently started selling these watches without the ability to buy spare charging pucks anywhere retail! The existing puck for Galaxy Watch 5/6/7 (and maybe 8? can't confirm) does NOT work with Watch 9 LTE. Comes up with a yellow triangle "incompatible charger" symbol. After time speaking on the phone with Samsung Customer Service I was able to order what is supposed to be one through Samsung Parts, run by Encompass (part# GH96-17240A). Having spare car & office pucks for a watch with a battery that only lasts for a day is crucial. I have two spare pucks for my old Galaxy Watch 5 Pro for that reason. UPDATE 9/23/26! THIS JUST GOT WORSE. No word on the Watch 9 charging puck order, so I called Samsung Parts for status to learn it is now BACKORDERED UNTIL 11/14/26 and worse they say that is just an estimate, could be longer. :( Two MONTHS from when I placed the order for something that should have been available when the watch came out. :( Wow. The alarm volume on the Watch 9 has turned out to be so soft I can barely hear it. I've had to go back to my old Watch 5 Pro for timing the yard sprinklers and such. I can hear that one in the next room. The "M/L" watch band is woefully short, as many others have posted now. It should be a "M". Samsung needs to make an "L" available and ideally an "XL". The band can be replaced for some other brand, but it is the principle of the thing. For $450, a large company like Samsung should have a properly sized watch bands available to ship with the watch. The Watch 5 Pro band has the same problem. Nothing screams "excess profit" like this issue, IMHO. :( The battery life is a joke, as many people have posted, lasting around 24 hours when many other watches will go for days. The battery life in my old Watch 5 Pro is even less, about 18 hours, so I figured that I would get used to it, but hasn't happened. Especially irritating knowing silicon carbon batteries with much greater capacity are out there. One of the reasons I hung on to my old Galaxy 5 Pro for so long is that the glass display is completely surrounded by round metal and therefore chip-proof. Well sure enough this display already has an edge chip on it. :( The Watch 9 does have a few good things still. I bought it to get LTE so I could make an emergency phone call if the phone isn't around. That still works via the Spectrum Mobile $11/month watch add-on plan. The Wi-Fi and Bluetooth versions are updated from the Watch 5 Pro and work better. And the biggee: the aluminum Watch 9 is light enough to wear all day long where the titanium Watch 5 Pro wasn't, without becoming annoying. But even then the Watch 9 LTE is 80% the same as the Watch 8 LTE! The case size, display, memory, and bio-sensors are all the same. Might was well get a cheaper (used, even) Watch 8 LTE to carry over to the watch 10 or 11. I'll be looking forward to trading-in this Watch 9 LTE the minute Samsung comes up with a bigger-battery LTE watch that will go a minimum of 2 days on a charge. Also looking for Watch 10 or 11 to have 5G rather than just LTE, Wi-Fi 7 & 6GHz vs. just Wi-Fi 6, and satellite communication - which the Snapdragon Wear Elite chip in it already supports. C'mon Samsung, time to step up your game here. :(

top_reviews.title: Outstanding!
top_reviews.variant: Color: Graphite Size: 40mm Style: Cellular Pattern Name: Watch9 Only
top_reviews.body: I bought this watch for my mom. She's 85 years old and has fallen a couple of times. She doesn't always carry her phone, which would enable her to call for help. This watch is a GREAT idea! I was able to put it on our phone carrier network (Patriot Mobile) very easily. Her phone is connected via Bluetooth to her phone, and it also has its own LTE data. So, if she happens to be away from her phone, she can still call for help. The watch is equipped with a fall detection function. It will automatically connect her to someone who can call 9/11 for her. She can make and answer calls just like a phone. It has so many other fantastic functions. I'm happy to say that it is user-friendly; probably one of the greatest features since Mom is 85. You can adjust the font size for better readability. It's durable and nice-looking. I actually purchased some stretchy nylon fabric bands so she is able to put in and remove it more easily than with the band it comes with. The 40mm is plenty large enough. The 44mm would be huge on her wrist. Definitely a worthwhile purchase!

top_reviews.title: Not Recommended. Wait for Galaxy Watch 10 or 11 LTE or get Watch 8 LTE.
top_reviews.variant: Color: Silver Size: 44mm Style: Cellular Pattern Name: Watch9 Only
top_reviews.body: Not recommended! I've had to change my opinion of the Galaxy Watch 9 LTE after some time with it. Best to wait for the Watch 10 or 11 LTE for hopefully a much bigger silicon-carbon battery and several other needed changes. The latest round is discovering Samsung apparently started selling these watches without the ability to buy spare charging pucks anywhere retail! The existing puck for Galaxy Watch 5/6/7 (and maybe 8? can't confirm) does NOT work with Watch 9 LTE. Comes up with a yellow triangle "incompatible charger" symbol. After time speaking on the phone with Samsung Customer Service I was able to order what is supposed to be one through Samsung Parts, run by Encompass (part# GH96-17240A). Having spare car & office pucks for a watch with a battery that only lasts for a day is crucial. I have two spare pucks for my old Galaxy Watch 5 Pro for that reason. UPDATE 9/23/26! THIS JUST GOT WORSE. No word on the Watch 9 charging puck order, so I called Samsung Parts for status to learn it is now BACKORDERED UNTIL 11/14/26 and worse they say that is just an estimate, could be longer. :( Two MONTHS from when I placed the order for something that should have been available when the watch came out. :( Wow. The alarm volume on the Watch 9 has turned out to be so soft I can barely hear it. I've had to go back to my old Watch 5 Pro for timing the yard sprinklers and such. I can hear that one in the next room. The "M/L" watch band is woefully short, as many others have posted now. It should be a "M". Samsung needs to make an "L" available and ideally an "XL". The band can be replaced for some other brand, but it is the principle of the thing. For $450, a large company like Samsung should have a properly sized watch bands available to ship with the watch. The Watch 5 Pro band has the same problem. Nothing screams "excess profit" like this issue, IMHO. :( The battery life is a joke, as many people have posted, lasting around 24 hours when many other watches will go for days. The battery life in my old Watch 5 Pro is even less, about 18 hours, so I figured that I would get used to it, but hasn't happened. Especially irritating knowing silicon carbon batteries with much greater capacity are out there. One of the reasons I hung on to my old Galaxy 5 Pro for so long is that the glass display is completely surrounded by round metal and therefore chip-proof. Well sure enough this display already has an edge chip on it. :( The Watch 9 does have a few good things still. I bought it to get LTE so I could make an emergency phone call if the phone isn't around. That still works via the Spectrum Mobile $11/month watch add-on plan. The Wi-Fi and Bluetooth versions are updated from the Watch 5 Pro and work better. And the biggee: the aluminum Watch 9 is light enough to wear all day long where the titanium Watch 5 Pro wasn't, without becoming annoying. But even then the Watch 9 LTE is 80% the same as the Watch 8 LTE! The case size, display, memory, and bio-sensors are all the same. Might was well get a cheaper (used, even) Watch 8 LTE to carry over to the watch 10 or 11. I'll be looking forward to trading-in this Watch 9 LTE the minute Samsung comes up with a bigger-battery LTE watch that will go a minimum of 2 days on a charge. Also looking for Watch 10 or 11 to have 5G rather than just LTE, Wi-Fi 7 & 6GHz vs. just Wi-Fi 6, and satellite communication - which the Snapdragon Wear Elite chip in it already supports. C'mon Samsung, time to step up your game here. :(

top_reviews.body: Soo, I waited a while before writing this. My goal buying the watch was health and fitness. The ultra 2 had the features that I wanted. top_reviews.title: Many, many amazing upgrades. Next level stuff, if you ask me.
top_reviews.variant: Color: Titanium Silver Size: 47mm Style: Cellular Pattern Name: Watch Ultra 2 Only
top_reviews.body: This device is a full improvement on the previous generation. Samsung took the time and listened to our input and fixed all the annoyances from the last watch and made this one the real MVP. It is a little bit larger than the last edition and it's screen is absolutely beautiful. According to NPR, this watch brings second in health accuracy, but that's not saying much when you consider that smart watches aren't really that accurate to begin with.. It's still good enough for what you need for baseline stuff.. Now let's talk about price. Samsung kept this device the same price as their last watch and I think that's phenomenal. I believe that it's worth every penny. There is one thing that I do not like about this watch though: The front bezel, while redesigned and it looks a lot nicer, unfortunately gets scratched up really easy. The Samsung Ultra Watch that I had for two years prior held up beautifully in my day-to-day welding work. This watch, however, the bezel is showing some pretty deep scratches after less than two months. If you're worried about that, they definitely sell protectors, but you shouldn't have to buy a protector for a watch that's labeled rugged. So, all in all. It's a big upgrade with a minor downgrade to durability.

It's still good enough for what you need for baseline stuff.. Now let's talk about price. Samsung kept this device the same price as their last watch and I think that's phenomenal. I believe that it's worth every penny. There is one thing that I do not like about this watch though: The front bezel, while redesigned and it looks a lot nicer, unfortunately gets scratched up really easy. The Samsung Ultra Watch that I had for two years prior held up beautifully in my day-to-day welding work. This watch, however, the bezel is showing some pretty deep scratches after less than two months. If you're worried about that, they definitely sell protectors, but you shouldn't have to buy a protector for a watch that's labeled rugged. So, all in all. It's a big upgrade with a minor downgrade to durability.
